newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call rate down as most banks square.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call rate down as most banks square.

text.p: The Philippine interbank call loan rate eased to 11.15625 percent on Friday from yesterday's 11.625 percent as most banks have already squared their positions for the end of the week, brokers said.
The Philippine Central Bank monitors banks' reserves positions on a weekly basis. It fines banks which are found to keep a deficient position for two consecutive weeks.
"Most of the big banks which were on the borrowing side have begun lending money today," one trader said.

He said big banks were borrowing aggressively on Thursday to ensure that they would not be deficient this week, since it would be very difficult to cover a deficient position next week due to a shortened work week.
Another trader said the heavy dollar selling yesterday also helped contribute to the liquidity of the domestic currency.
Done rates ranged from a low of 10.8125 percent to a high of 12.125 percent. Turnover dwindled to only 17.594 billion pesos.
The secondary market for government securities was swamped with sellers who wanted funds in order to stay liquid during the New Year weekend.
"Some banks were selling their short-term bills, but there was a dearth of buyers," a trader said.
Three-month bills were being bid between 11.525 to 11.825 percent and offered between 11.425 to 11.725 percent.

Six-month bills were being bought between 11.80 to 12.0 percent, and sold between 11.70 to 11.90 percent. One-year bills were being bid between 12.15 to 13.0 percent and offered between 12.05 to 12.60 percent. - RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 63 2 8418938
